source_title: ThreatsDay: AI Secrets Leak, PingCAP Source Theft, Signal Hang-Up Flaw, Laravel Auth Bypass + 21 More
source_excerpt:
This week has already been rough for cybersecurity. Critical PHP and GitLab RCE flaws, serious Linux security bugs , compromised eMudhra certificates , a Node.js RCE flaw , a hacked LiteLLM release, and hundreds of hijacked Tor relays . That's a lot to deal with in just a few days. And the week isn't even over yet.
But those big headlines are only half the story. Stolen passwords, exposed databases, broken login checks, and trusted tools being turned against their users are causing trouble too. Some attacks are clever. Others work because someone left a simple security gap open.
This ThreatsDay, we're digging into the stories that didn't make as much noise but still deserve attention. Some are strange, some are serious, and a few might surprise you. Here's everything else you shouldn't miss this week.
The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.
4,500+ accounts compromised Bluesky Confirms More Than 4,500 Accounts Compromised in Phishing Campaign Bluesky has acknowledged it's aware of a phishing attack that has compromised more than 4,500 accounts. "The attack spread through posts promoting a fake offer of a government payment," Bluesky said . "We have temporarily suspended the compromised accounts and are working with their owners to secure them and restore access. If your account was suspended, email moderation@blueskyweb.xyz and we will help to get you back into your account."

Android malware scam losses Singapore Police Warn of Android Malware Scams Causing Nearly S$1 Million in Losses The Singapore Police Force has alerted users of a malware-enabled scam variant involving advertisements on social media platforms promoting senior-focused activities and programmes, water-based fitness activities, and recycling initiatives. The agency said at least 62 cases have been reported since April 2026, leading to S$989,000 in losses. "In this scam, victims would come across the fake advertisements on social media platforms, such as Facebook, and be instructed to download an Android Application Package (APK) file to facilitate programme registration or service arrangements," the Singapore Police Force said . "After installing the application, victims would receive unsolicited calls from scammers impersonating government officials or bank representatives, who would falsely claim that the victims' devices or bank accounts had been compromised, or that they were implicated in criminal activities. Victims would then be induced to transfer monies, disclose banking credentials or personal information, or surrender valuables for investigations."

Customer credentials exposed Andromeda Confirms Credential Theft Affecting AI Infrastructure Customers Andromeda said it identified a security incident on October 13, 2026, that involved unauthorized access to credentials in its environment. "We disabled the compromised accounts that day and have observed no further unauthorized activity since," it said . "We believe the activity began as part of an industry-wide attack on or about October 9th. It affected a limited number of customer accounts and involved exposure of certain Andromeda and customer credentials. If we believe you were affected, you’ve already heard from us." The company said there is no evidence of unauthorized access to customer models, datasets, or training data.

20 security flaws patched Roundcube Fixes 20 Security Issues Including IMAP Injection and SSRF Bypass Roundcube has released versions 1.6.20 and 1.7.5, addressing 20 issues including IMAP command injection, SSRF filter bypass, and unsafe attachment handling. There is no evidence any of the patched vulnerabilities have been exploited.

Internal business systems breached Genesys Confirms Breach of Internal CRM and Learning Systems On October 16, 2026, Genesys disclosed that it became aware of a cybersecurity incident involving an unauthorized third party that allowed them to access certain internal business systems, including a learning management system (LMS) and a customer relationship management (CRM) platform. The company said business and account information used to manage relationships with existing and prospective customers has been accessed and/or downloaded without authorization. However, it said its Genesys Cloud, Genesys Engage and Genesys Engage Cloud platforms were not compromised.

Critical Kubernetes host takeover risk NVIDIA AIStore Flaw Reportedly Allows Kubernetes Host Takeover AegisSec Research has disclosed details of a NVIDIA AIStore for Linux flaw present in the legacy ETL Kubernetes PodSpec initialization API, CVE-2026-65162 aka ShadowForge (CVSS score: 10.0), that enables privileged container creation and host-level compromise.

NFC bank fraud arrests Dutch Police Arrest Two Suspects in NFC Bank Card Relay Fraud Scheme Dutch police authorities have arrested two suspects in connection with a bank helpdesk fraud scheme that netted 170 victims and €380,000 in illicit proceeds. The arrested men include a 23-year-old from Vaassen and a 25-year-old from Ede. "Victims were called on their phones and played an audio clip," authorities said . "The scammers had created dozens of different audio clips using Artificial Intelligence, featuring various voices, banks, companies, and scenarios. The voice would, for example, alert them to suspicious activity on their bank account [and instruct them to] download an app and scan their bank card by holding it against their phone." In the process, the threat actors were able to forward the data from the bank card's NFC chip to the threat actor, who then used it to make unauthorized withdrawals.

Critical API authentication bypass Laravel Patches Critical TokenGuard Flaw Allowing API Authentication Bypass Laravel has patched a critical security flaw (CVE-2026-114509, CVSS score: 9.2) that could allow its built-in TokenGuard to be bypassed to authenticate as an arbitrary existing user without knowledge of their valid API token. "Under certain database configurations (MySQL/MariaDB), an attacker can submit a specially crafted, non-string credential value that is mishandled during the authentication lookup, causing the underlying query to match an unintended user record rather than failing authentication as expected," Laravel said . "An unauthenticated attacker may authenticate as another user without possessing that user's API token, leading to authentication bypass and account takeover on any route protected by the affected guard." The issue has been patched in versions 13.29.0 and 12.68.0.

Critical unauthenticated RCE risk Critical Eptura Archibus Flaws Allow Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution Rapid7 said it discovered three new vulnerabilities in Eptura Archibus that could be exploited to achieve code execution. "A legacy API endpoint could be exploited to bypass authentication and run various functions without authentication (CVE-2026-107186, CVSS: 8.6 High)," it said . "The most serious functions allow for full database read (CVE-2026-107187, CVSS: 8.5 High) and an insecure file upload (CVE-2026-107188, CVSS: 9.6 Critical). The insecure file upload leads to remote code execution. A malicious actor with network access to the server via HTTP can read secrets and passwords out of the database. They can also run code to execute system commands as 'NT AUTHORITY/Local Service' and gain control of the server."

3.2 million secrets exposed Zeabur to Shut Down After Second Cyber Attack Exposes Customer Secrets Development platform Zeabur said it will shut down its services starting December 1, 2026, and finish by December 31, 2026, in response to a cybersecurity incident in which attackers leaked internal credentials stored in plaintext to compromise its infrastructure and steal over 3.2 million environment variable records and information for 321,810 accounts. "On October 14–15, 2026, an attacker used leaked Zeabur internal credentials to break into the shared cluster, some Dedicated Servers, and Zeabur internal systems, and eventually read the platform database," according to an announcement. This is the second time Zeabur has suffered a breach this year alone. In August 2026, the company said an attacker gained unauthorized access to its systems and stole sensitive data, including account information, API keys, and other secrets.

Source code and customer data stolen PingCAP Confirms Source Code Theft and Exposure of TiDB Cloud Customer Information PingCAP has disclosed that attackers used stolen credentials to access internal systems and copy source code and customer-related records, including SQL editor content and encrypted API-key values. The incident took place between September 9 and October 7, 2026. "An unauthorized party used stolen service account credentials to access certain PingCAP internal systems, copy data, and obtain source code," the company said . "PingCAP became aware of the incident on October 7 and began disabling the affected credentials the same day." Exported data includes user names and email addresses, organization and project associations, SQL editor text and errors, customer contacts, contract terms, orders, pricing, payment terms, and billing configuration.

$2.5 million tax fraud scheme Nigerian Man Sentenced To Eight Years for Identity Theft Scheme Chukwuemeka Victor Amachukwu (aka Chukwuemeka Victor Eletuo and So Kwan Leung), a 40-year-old Nigerian national, has been sentenced to eight years in prison in the U.S. for running a years-long hacking, tax fraud, and identity theft scheme. "Amachukwu took part in sophisticated schemes to hack into U.S. businesses, steal and use stolen identity information of victims, and commit fraud," the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) said . "Beginning in at least in or about 2019, Amachukwu, his co-conspirator Kinglsey Uchelue Utulu, and other Nigeria-based conspirators took part in a scheme to hack into U.S-based tax preparation businesses. The conspirators utilized spear-phishing emails to obtain access to these businesses' electronic systems. Once they had obtained access, the conspirators stole the tax and other identifying information for at least approximately 800 of the business's customers. The conspirators hacked into several U.S. based tax businesses, located in New York, Texas, and other states." The conspirators also obtained the stolen identity information of thousands of individuals and then used this information to file fraudulent tax returns with the Internal Revenue Service and state tax authorities, obtaining at least approximately $2.5 million.

Military identity theft scheme Philippines-Based American Fraudster Pleads Guilty to Fraud Robert Wayne Boling, a 45-year-old U.S. citizen, pleaded guilty to running an identity theft and fraud scheme that defrauded thousands of U.S. service members and veterans while living in the Philippines. "Boling operated from the Philippines, and he received and exploited stolen personally identifiable information (PII) of U.S. servicemembers and veterans to compromise their bank accounts and steal money and veterans' benefits," the DoJ said . "Boling's co-conspirator, Fredrick Brown, who worked as a civilian medical records administrator for the U.S. Army in South Korea, took digital photographs of the PII of thousands of military-affiliated individuals. Brown provided the stolen PII to Boling, who, along with his co-conspirators, used the PII to compromise various accounts belonging to U.S. servicemembers and veterans, including bank accounts and online government-affiliated benefits accounts." Boling pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering. He is scheduled to be sentenced on January 14, 2027, and faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison for each conspiracy charge.

$6 million data breach settlement 23andMe Settles with California Over 2023 Breach Chrome Holding Co., a holding company formerly known as 23andMe, has agreed to pay California $6 million to resolve accusations that it did not effectively secure customers' personal and genetic data, resulting in a massive 2023 breach that exposed sensitive information belonging to nearly 7 million people. "With regard to the genetic data or samples maintained by 23andMe Research Institute, consumers can request that the company delete their data, destroy their test sample, or revoke their permission for their genetic data to be used for research," the office of the California Attorney General said in a statement.
